_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FN] The Aztec ruin kind (Mike, 9 and 10 Oct, design §FN, bones plus what he specified). Claude (chat) wrote it; nothing reads it yet, and Claude Code removes this prefix as each block is wired (queues 78-84, docs/PROMPT_QUEUE.md). A line marked 'mike' is his; a line marked 'claude_guess' is Claude's first guess for Claude Code to tune by eye and Mike to settle by playing; 'open' is not decided (§FN.8). It is additive: it changes no existing file, and it is the Aztec ruin's own, so nothing here is read for another ruin kind.
_help.kind: temple, not a tomb (§FN.1): no sarcophagi and no burial chambers; the mummy and sarcophagi move to a new Egyptian ruin (§FN.0). world: assumed desert, because the snake is the desert's boss and the surface was built as desert (worlds.json surface.world); open, §FN.8 call 1, since the plants of this ruin do not grow in hot desert.
_help.stone: One ruin, one stone (§EX.1): the temple needs its own masonry.json style (queue 79). andean_tomb is Inca fitted polygonal stone and belongs to the Inca ruin, not this one.
_help.calendar: The tonalpohualli (§FN.1): 20 day signs in the standard order, each with a number 1-13 written as dots. The order here is the one the 9 Oct research gave; Mexicolore lists the signs in a different order, so check against a museum source before carving them in a fixed sequence. The English names are Claude's own knowledge.
_help.chambers: The two fixed main chambers (Mike, 10 Oct): in every Aztec temple, where they sit and how they are joined coming from the dungeon's seed (§FK.2) over room_pool.json's rules. Which floor holds each: open (§FN.8 call 8).
_help.floors: Two or three per ruin, drawn by the dungeon's seed (§FN.3). descent.json floors.count stays 2 until queue 81 builds a third.
_help.snake: The desert boss (bosses.json bosses.desert, boss_pool.json pools.desert) becomes the feathered serpent (§FN.2). This block adds a look and a sound; it replaces none of the snake's behaviour (queues 49, 57, 65, 66).
_help.enabled: (Claude Code, queue 80, design §FN.1, §FN.8 call 1) Whether the Aztec temple is in the game. false (the default): no game draws it, and the first ruin is the tomb exactly as before. Set true 12 Oct (Mike: "azetec should be activated to be able to spawn there"): a new game's first ruin may be the temple; answers enough of §FN.8 call 1 to switch it on; which biome world is still open, it keeps the desert surface queue 84 gave it. true: the temple joins §FJ.1's roster (crawler.json opening_pick): a new game's first ruin is the tomb or the temple, drawn from the game's seed. It chooses no biome world: which world it sits in is Mike's call. Restart after editing.
_help.chambers_built: (Claude Code, queue 80) Built: room_pool.json archetypes aztec_blood_altar and aztec_calendar_room (always true), one of each in every temple, both on floor one (floor_as_built; which floor holds each is open, §FN.8 call 8). The temple itself is the tomb generator (TombKit) in masonry.json's aztec_temple stone, crawler.json themes.aztec_temple.
_help.world_answered: (Claude Code, 12 Oct, design §FN.8 call 1) Mike: "the mid Mexico biome is the Aztec"; "Aztec is not cloud forest. it should be montane grasslands/shrublands". world: worlds.json worlds.aztec_highland (biome montane_grassland, data/biomes/52_montane_grassland.json); the surface over the temple grows it (worlds.json surface.by_theme.aztec_temple); the tomb's surface stays the desert. The kind line's 'assumed desert' is out of date.
_help.surface: The Aztec silhouette on the surface (§FN.4): a step pyramid with an altar at the top, ambient, never a fast-travel point.

world_status: answered 12 Oct (Mike, §FN.8 call 1): the central Mexican montane grassland and shrubland

stone.claude_guess: plastered and painted in life, mostly red; a ruin now keeps dark bare stone with the red left only in the recesses
stone.note: the real analogue is the Templo Mayor of Tenochtitlan

calendar.temple_style: carved day-sign panels with dot numerals (mike: 'tonalpohualli for Aztec style temple thing')
calendar.claude_guess_structural_count: 13 as the count of tiers or stair steps; not confirmed
calendar.snake_sign: Coatl (snake), the boss room's sign (Claude's suggestion, 9 Oct)
calendar.luck_of_numbers: not used: a deeper source says luck belonged to particular days, not to numbers

chambers.placement: seeded (the dungeon's seed, §FK.2); the other rooms and ways are the pool's generic ones, shuffled per run (room_pool.json)

blood_altar.mike: a circular sacrificial blood altar, in its own chamber
blood_altar.model: the round Aztec sacrificial stone (temalacatl): a low carved drum with a ring of relief round the rim

claude_guess.stain: dried, near-black brown, never bright red (fire is the one warm accent)
claude_guess.props: a stone bowl beside it, offerings, copal braziers; no bodies
claude_guess.reason: the Templo Mayor dig found thousands of offerings and few human remains (a strong, partly disputed argument); dread through atmosphere, never gore (§FG)

calendar_room.mike: the Aztec calendar has its own room; flavour for now, no puzzle
calendar_room.holds: the tonalpohualli carved in full: the 20 day signs and the 13 dot numerals
calendar_room.hidden_carvings: some carvings are only seen under the brew (§FN.5, data/visions.json)

floors.third_floor: same stone, goes further (§FM.6); whether it is darker again: open
floors.way_on: light every torch on a floor and the way on opens (§FN.3); on floor one both ways at once (§FM.6, descent.json fork)
floors.cue: audio.json stone_seal, the grinding of the seal sinking, for every floor's seal; whether it carries to the surface: open (§FN.8 call 4)

snake.mike: give the snake feathers like Quetzalcoatl, for the historical accuracy of their legends; it needs a rattle

plumes.claude_guess: iridescent green and turquoise, with a little red toward the breast (quetzal feathers are green with a red breast)

rattle.mike: Quetzalcoatl is like a giant rattlesnake; currently the snake has no rattle
rattle.evidence: the earliest feathered serpents (Olmec) are crested rattlesnakes, taken by scholars as the prototype (Wikipedia, Feathered Serpent: Nicholson, Taube); the sources opened do not show rattles on Aztec or Teotihuacan serpents specifically
rattle.tail: a rattle at the tail tip on the body bake
rattle.sound: a dry shiver, new, beside snake_warn and snake_hiss
rattle.claude_guess_when: sounds when it holds off at your flame (torch_delay), so the sharp hiss still always means the strike (§FA.2); its roaming tell stays scales on stone

snake.fireless: the xiuhcoatl is a different, fire serpent; this snake breathes no fire and the volcano's dragon stays the one fire-breather

lair.mike: the whole ruin is the snake's lair, based on the holes in the walls it creeps through
lair.holes_run_through: the whole temple, every floor it can reach
lair.open: how this sits with the single lair hole of §EY.3 and the base layer of §FM.1 (§FN.8 call 3); assumed: the wall-holes are its roads and the lair hole is where the last light drives it

surface.mike: all the ruins underground need a counterpart on the surface; ambient world building, not a fast-travel landmark
surface.silhouette: step pyramid with an altar at the top
surface.come_up: inside it or beside it: open
surface.two_altars: the summit altar above and the round blood altar below are read as two places; open (§FN.8 call 5)
surface.other_cultures: flagged only (mike: just flagging it for now); no other silhouette is assigned and none is to be drawn until he asks

pyramid._help: (Claude Code, queue 84, design §FN.4; first guesses, tune by eye) The step pyramid over the Aztec temple (AztecPyramid), built only while enabled is true and the dungeon is the temple. tiers: how many (13 is the calendar's count, a guess not confirmed; 5 reads as a ruin's mound at this size); base_m: the lowest tier's side; tier_h_m: each tier's height; inset_m: how far each tier steps in; stair_w_m: the stair's width up the face toward where you come up; stair_slope: its rise over its run (0.6, the tomb's own stairs, walkable); altar_m: the altar block on the top [wide, high, deep]; crumble: the share of each tier's top course settled, askew or gone (more at the corners); at_m: how far from where you come up it stands [nearest, furthest tried]; off_deg: how far off the way you face [least, most], so it stands beside the way out's line, in view, out of the wash. Scenery only: no exit, no beacon, no fast travel, no gameplay number.
